description: Impacts of Herbicide Brush Management on Hydrology & Sedimentation at Walnut Gulch Experimental Watershed is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The conversion of grassland ecosystems has important ecological and economic consequences, including the loss of fertile topsoil, vegetation cover, and associated habitat and forage values. Shrub management strategies like herbicide treatments seek to reduce woody plant cover to allow for the recovery of grasslands. Coverage: Walnut Gulch, Arizona (2022). The toolkit gives Walnut Gulch, Arizona as the location, 2022 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
